prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses is a current charge to earnings made in order to adjust the allowance for credit losses for current expected losses in the loan portfolio based on an evaluation of the loan portfolio characteristics, current economic conditions, changes in the nature and volume of lending, historical loan experience and other known internal and external factors affecting loan collectability, and assessment of reasonable and supportable forecasts of future economic conditions that would impact collectability of the loans. Our allowance for credit losses is calculated by segmenting the loan portfolio by loan type and applying risk factors to each segment. The risk factors are determined by considering historical loss data, peer data, as well as applying management’s judgment.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, we had a provision for credit losses of $1 million and for the three months ended September 30, 2025, we had a recovery of credit losses of $49 thousand. The provision during the three months ended September 30, 2026 was driven by $33 million of growth in the loan portfolio in the third quarter of 2026, concentrated in loans secured by real estate.

nonint.text: Noninterest expenses increased 15% to $37 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $32 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher salaries and benefits expenses, occupancy expenses, and miscellaneous lending expenses, partially offset by lower professional fees, FDIC insurance expense, and data processing expense.

nonop.text: Our operating results depend primarily on our net interest income, which is the difference between interest and dividend income on interest-earning assets such as loans and investments, and interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities such as deposits and borrowings.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text:
Three-Month Comparison Net income available to common shareholders for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $9 million, or $0.35 basic and diluted earnings per share, compared to $7 million, or $0.28 basic and diluted earnings per share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The results reflect strong growth in net interest income of $7 million driven by growth in interest income and flat interest expense. We also experienced a $1 million increase in noninterest income driven by increased loan sale gains and higher income from bank-owned life insurance. These increases were offset by higher noninterest expense driven by personnel costs and occupancy expenses, the former due to growth in PMC and Mortgage Warehouse and the latter primarily a result of higher lease expense due to the sale-leaseback transaction executed in December 2025. Additional details of the changes in net income will be discussed in the remaining sections of this Results of Operations section.

Nine-Month Comparison Net income available to common shareholders for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $25 million, or $1.03 basic and diluted earnings per share, compared to $32 million, or $1.29 basic and diluted earnings per share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin
Net interest income.text: Our operating results depend primarily on our net interest income, which is the difference between interest and dividend income on interest-earning assets such as loans and investments, and interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities such as deposits and borrowings.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest income increased 8% to $13 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher gain on sale of loans in the current year, an increase in bank-owned life insurance income and a loan recovery gain in other noninterest income, partially offset by lower mortgage banking income and losses on other investments in the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Noninterest income had a $1 million increase in gains on sale of loans year-over-year primarily driven by $32 million of sales of Panacea Division commercial loans to another financial institution generating over $600 thousand of gains and the sale of the guaranteed portion of $12 million of SBA loans generating $1 million in gains. We continue to experience increases in bank-owned life insurance income as a result of a restructuring of that portfolio, which is expected to be completed in the last quarter of 2026, and a $400 thousand death benefit received during the quarter. Noninterest income in the third quarter of 2026 also benefited from $1 million in recoveries on a loan that was charged-off by a predecessor bank, recorded in other noninterest income.

intro.text: Primis Financial Corp. is the bank holding company for Primis Bank, a Virginia state-chartered bank which commenced operations on April 14, 2005. Primis Bank provides a range of financial services to individuals and small and medium-sized businesses. As of December 31, 2025, Primis had $4.0 billion in total assets, $3.3 billion in total loans held for investment, $3.4 billion in total deposits and $423 million in total stockholders’ equity. As of December 31, 2025, Primis Bank had 24 full-service branches in Virginia and Maryland and also provides services to customers through certain online and mobile applications. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, the Company has an administrative office in Glen Allen, Virginia and an operations center in Atlee, Virginia. PMC, a residential mortgage lender headquartered in Wilmington, North Carolina, is a consolidated subsidiary of Primis Bank.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
